Pool edit checked with git diff before booting: exactly one line changed in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt, '# clock_getres01' -> 'clock_getres01', matching pool_entries exactly. clock_getres01 appears in no blocked/ file, so nothing else is blocked in this pool file under the default configuration and still_blocked_absent is trivially true; separately confirmed no non-enabled testcase appeared in the run output, so the blocklist filtering was not bypassed.

One apparent regression was investigated and ruled out as a flake. The first full-suite run with the fix showed prctl02 going pass -> skip against the previous run's stored log (Skipped 65 vs 52). Three checks cleared it: (1) the patch is entirely clock-scoped -- it touches no prctl, seccomp, capability or THP code, and the x86 syscall table is explicitly numbered rather than positional, so inserting SYS_CLOCK_GETRES = 229 cannot shift any other syscall number; (2) prctl02 passes in an isolated selector run on the fixed kernel; (3) most conclusively, I stashed the kernel half of the patch and ran a true baseline full suite at this run's own base commit e8f2b9ca6 with only the all.txt edit in place -- prctl02 passed there, and the only status difference from the fixed run was clock_getres01 fail -> skip. A second full-suite run with the fix restored (patch verified byte-identical to the pre-stash patch) again showed prctl02 passing. prctl02's TCONF branches are probe-driven (setup() probes PR_GET_SECCOMP, PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, PR_GET_THP_DISABLE, PR_CAP_AMBIENT, PR_GET_SPECULATION_CTRL and marks each unsupported on EINVAL), which is a plausible source of run-to-run variation independent of this change. The verified figures above are from the reproducible second run; the first run's own numbers were Passed 2667 / Failed 0 / Broken 0 / Skipped 65 / Warnings 0, also green.

The earlier 52-skip figure came from run-atDPcd, whose base 68bdd4a99 is a parallel branch and not an ancestor of e8f2b9ca6 (merge-base 8a9543109), so its skip counts are not a valid baseline for this run; that is why I measured a fresh baseline at e8f2b9ca6 rather than reasoning from the stored one.

Baseline at e8f2b9ca6 without the kernel fix: Passed 2617 / Failed 10 / Broken 0 / Skipped 54, make exit 2, with 'clock_getres01: fail' as the sole failing test -- reproducing diagnose.json's 10 failures precisely and confirming the fix is what turns the suite green.

Unrelated pre-existing observation, not caused by this change: munmap02 is enabled in all.txt (545 uncommented entries) but never appears in the run output (Runs: 544). It is absent from the baseline log and from run-atDPcd's log too, so it predates this run; worth a look in a future round.
